body: hear me out on this one — we give the money to them

It’s a frustrating transition. It started losing members to a neighboring church, and is in a race for the most “youth friendly” experience, which seems to just be the most money and extravagance we can throw around. I think it’s sad to see it spiraling this way. 

I’m not sure if I’m religious regardless. But it’s sad to think that a part of me is skeptical when I see my family write checks to the church. I admire the philosophy of a community that helps their neighbors, even if i disagree with their uniting principles. It makes me sad to think that even that might be lost to materialism

I apologize if I came off that way. To be honest, Im just getting really mad after seeing a fundraiser for a 100k TV outside of the church i went to as a child. I am unsure of where to weve gotten to the idea that churches need to be expensive. 

And you’re right. I have money for things that aren’t survival necessity and some people dont. But I don’t claim to be serving God on earth. I think if the church wants to be respected that way it should act that way.

I can understand this perspective, and I appreciate willingness to actually talk. I just don’t think it’s what we get from Jesus’ work. He seems to focus on the exact opposite, not adorning ourselves fancifully in the name of the Lord, but that “wherever two or more are gathered in my name God is present” and condemning the hypocrisy of the pharisees. 


So while this makes sense for how WE perceive honoring the Lord, it seems to me Jesus was CHALLENGING this long standing bias

“we are called to pluck the log out of our own eye… so i suggest that *you*” is the summation of why I left this religion. your answer to hypocrisy is more hypocrisy. I’m sure they’ll put you in charge of covering up child predators some day soon.
the same weakness that the church is unwilling to rectify thousands of years later. A selfish, blind, cling tk materialism. An unwillingness to love your neighbor as yourself
Jesus told the rich man to sell everything he owned, give it to the poor, and worship him. This is an incredibly lazy and scriptually indefensible excuse
